title: Final: many threads
sub: Races, locks and the pool: test yourself
cards/0/task: Show a lost update: get count to end at 1.
cards/1/explain: Three separate steps, and the thread can be interrupted between any of them.
cards/2/task: Fix the deadlock and run both threads to completion.
cards/3/q: What do threads share? Select all that apply.
cards/3/explain: Each thread has its own stack and everything on it.
cards/4/q: You just need to count requests from many threads. What do you pick?
cards/4/options/1: A lock around the whole request handler
cards/4/explain: Interlocked solves it with a single instruction and makes nobody wait.
cards/5/explain: Anyone who uses the object has a reference to it and can take the same lock. A private readonly lock object is better.
cards/6/q: The CPU is idle, yet requests sit in the pool queue. Most likely…
cards/6/options/2: The garbage collector is turned off
cards/6/explain: Thread pool starvation: the threads exist, but they're waiting instead of working.
cards/7/task: Serve 8 requests without a single thread stuck waiting.
cards/8/q: Two threads read the same immutable string. Do you need synchronization?
cards/8/options/0: No: races only happen when something writes
cards/8/explain: If nobody changes the data, any number of threads can read it.
